biography.plain_text: Thomas Edward Brodie Sopwith, known as Tommy, was a British motor trader and racing driver. He built Endeavour Motor Company into a major Sussex dealership group, then developed Rivervale after selling the Ford business. Through Endeavour Holdings, he retained ownership of the later vehicle sales and leasing business until his death.

long_biography.plain_text:
While apprenticed to Armstrong Siddeley, racing driver Tommy Sopwith had the Sphinx built to compete with purpose-built sports cars. Its Allard chassis carried a modified Armstrong Siddeley engine, and factory employees worked on it in their spare time. The car gave his Equipe Endeavour team victories against Jaguar opposition.

In 1958, he won eight rounds of the inaugural British Saloon Car Championship but finished level on points with Jack Sears, who competed in a smaller class. Two identical Rileys settled the title in a deciding contest, which Sears won. Sopwith subsequently ran cars for other drivers, helped organise the London-Sydney Marathon and later chaired the British Racing Drivers' Club.
